entities.summary: Peter Johann Christoph Graf von der Pahlen was a Baltic German aristocrat and a general of the Imperial Russian Army. Born into the nobility of Livonia, he graduated from the Imperial Russian Military College and joined the army in 1835. Von der Pahlen served in the Crimean War, distinguishing himself in the Siege of Sevastopol, and was promoted to general in 1855. He played a key role in the suppression of the Polish November Uprising in 1831 and was awarded the Order of Saint Stanislaus. After the war, he retired to his estates in Livonia and died on May 1, 1864. His legacy as a military leader and administrator continues to be studied by historians of the Russian Empire.
